recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (11): github.com/gotify/server/v3/api.NewOIDC: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v3/api.OIDCAPI.LoginHandler: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v3/api.OIDCAPI: layout of compiled-in type OIDCAPI changed (1 functions use it); S6 replaces functions, not types; github.com/gotify/server/v3/config.Get: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v3/config.parseList: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; ... and 6 more
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: github.com/gotify/server/v3/ui.Register is exported: callers outside the analysed module are not in the closure
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 9 functions
type information is partial (359/363 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
